# Copy-ZbxHost

## SYNOPSIS

Copies a host to a new name on the same server.

## SYNTAX

```
Copy-ZbxHost [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>> [-NewName] <string> [-Force] [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Copy-ZbxHost cmdlet exports the host in -InputObject with configuration.export, renames the document to -NewName, points its graphs and trigger expressions at the copy, and imports it with configuration.import. The copy gets the host's items, triggers, graphs, discovery rules, macros, tags and interfaces; a calculated item's formula that names the original host is copied unchanged. With -Force a host already named -NewName is updated from the copy; without it only what is missing is created. The command writes the copy only with -PassThru.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Copy a host

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' | Copy-ZbxHost -NewName 'web-02' -PassThru | Select-Object TechnicalName, HostId
```

The copy takes web-01's groups, interfaces, items and triggers under the name web-02.

### Example 2: Copy a host and check what came along

```powershell
Copy-ZbxHost 'web-01' 'web-03'
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-03' | Select-Object Key, Type
```

-InputObject (position 0) and -NewName (position 1) are positional; the copy's items are the host's.
